name: Serbia
summary: An independent kingdom from 1878, part of Yugoslavia from 1918 to 1992, then of Serbia and Montenegro, and independent again since 2006.

knownFor.label: Nikola Tesla
knownFor.note: Serb-American inventor of AC electrical systems.

location.value: Central Balkans, landlocked; about 77,000 km² (excluding Kosovo).

terrain.value: Pannonian plain in the north, mountains in the south.

climate.value: Continental, with hot summers and cold winters, and a milder climate in the south.

resources.value: Farmland, copper (Bor), coal and rivers for hydropower.

disasters.value: Severe floods in 2014 hit the Sava and Morava valleys.

population.value: About 6.6 million people (excluding Kosovo), and falling slowly.

urbanisation.value: Belgrade is the only city with more than a million people, about four times larger than any other.

disease.value: Life expectancy is about 76 years, below the EU average.

migration.value: During and after the Second World War, tens of thousands of Serb refugees and more than 200,000 settlers came from Croatia and Bosnia.

economicBase.value: Farming, cars (Fiat), mining, IT and services.

tradeRoutes.value: The Danube and main road and rail routes between Central Europe and Greece.

moneyAndTax.value: The Serbian dinar; the first dinar was introduced in 1868.

inequality.value: Large gaps between Belgrade and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A parliamentary republic with an elected president.

keyRulers.value: Prince Miloš Obrenović. King Peter I. Slobodan Milošević. Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Monarchy, then part of Yugoslavia, elections since 1990.

institutions.value: National Assembly; critics say media and courts are under government pressure.

stability.value: The NATO bombing of 1999 and the long dispute over Kosovo.

eliteConflict.value: Dominance of the Serbian Progressive Party since 2012; large protests in 2024–25.

armyAndTech.value: Militarily neutral; buys arms from both Russia and the West.

majorWars.value: Balkan Wars, First World War (Sarajevo 1914), Yugoslav wars.

territoryChange.value: Kosovo declared independence in 2008; Serbia does not recognise it.

alliancesRivals.value: Candidate for the EU; close ties with Russia and China.

inventions.value: No major inventions are recorded for the state itself.

scienceEducation.value: University of Belgrade (1808); Nikola Tesla was a Serb from Croatia.

openness.value: Varied: open to trade with the EU, Russia and China, but cautious in politics.

communicationTransport.value: Motorways and a new high-speed railway to Novi Sad.

languageWriting.value: Serbian, written in both Cyrillic and Latin script.

artsArchitecture.value: Medieval monasteries (Studenica), the films of Emir Kusturica.

socialStructure.value: A Serb majority, with minorities speaking Hungarian (2.5%), Bosnian (2.2%), Romani (1.2%) and other languages.

sharedIdentity.value: Orthodox faith and the memory of Kosovo (Battle of Kosovo, 1389).

dailyLife.value: Apartments and houses; ćevapi, ajvar, rakija.

neighbours.value: Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, North Macedonia, Bosnia, Croatia, Montenegro.

riseSignals.value: Autonomy within the Ottoman Empire (1815) and full independence at the Congress of Berlin (1878).

declineSignals.value: Sanctions and the wars of the 1990s damaged the economy and isolated the country.

outcome.value: Serbia continues as an independent republic.
